problem: 'Verified by computer far beyond 10^18' overstates the record: Oliveira e Silva, Herzog and Pardi (2014) verified it up to 4·10^18.
corrected: Every even integer greater than $2$ is a sum of two primes (Goldbach to Euler, 1742). Verified by computer up to $4\cdot 10^{18}$; the ternary version was proved by Helfgott in 2013.

problem: Natural proofs is a conditional barrier (it assumes strong pseudorandom functions exist), and the barriers rule out classes of techniques, so 'provably cannot settle it' is too strong as stated.
corrected: Is every problem whose solutions can be checked in polynomial time also solvable in polynomial time? Most researchers expect $\mathrm P \ne \mathrm{NP}$; the barrier results on relativisation, natural proofs and algebrisation show that broad classes of known techniques cannot settle it (the natural-proofs barrier assumes strong pseudorandom functions exist).

problem: BSD concerns elliptic curves; for a general plane cubic, deciding whether it has a rational point at all is not addressed by the conjecture.
corrected: It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems and would give an algorithm for deciding whether an elliptic curve over $\mathbb Q$ has infinitely many rational points.
